# Plan: implemented commands in saved-import guidance

Correct the saved-patch explanation without changing recovery behavior. This is a guidance-only fix for issue and PR runs; no command, patch execution, permission, format, authority, or provenance changes.

## Dimensions

Approved dimensions: small / known / standard; compact profile. One implementation and validation cycle fits the 16-hour claim budget.

## What we know

- `internal/workflow/import_policy.go:204` (`recoveryReason`) emits unsupported issue/PR `recover-import` instructions whenever a patch was saved. It already projects only `filepath.Base`, and the unavailable-patch branch uses a fixed note.
- `internal/workflow/import_policy.go:171` (`importRejectionReason`) supplies real `work --phase implement` retries, unchanged-worktree context, role-output explanations and instruction flags. Eligible tester retries independently use `--phase test`; preserve that behavior.
- Actual command trees are registered at `internal/cli/root.go:123`, `internal/cli/issue.go:195`, and `internal/cli/pr.go:43`. Work flags exist at `internal/cli/work.go:207` and `internal/cli/pr.go:287`; neither group registers recover-import.
- `internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go:126` and `:201` explicitly expect the invented commands. The former also verifies private path placement, saved patch metadata/body, and absence of imported artifacts.
- `internal/workflow/import_policy_test.go:58` covers recoverability, roles, protected inputs and fork rejection. `internal/agent/recovery_test.go:62` covers private storage.
- Repository search found additional unsupported command claims only in comments at `internal/workflow/import_policy.go:25`, `:137`, and `internal/agent/recovery.go:18` (besides tests intentionally forbidding the string).

## What we're assuming

A maintainer can inspect saved text and supply reviewed guidance through existing work instruction flags; this does not authorize or apply the patch. Flag registration was verified in source. Exact final prose may be adjusted while retaining all asserted semantics.

## Open questions

None affecting scope. The exposed snapshot has no Git metadata (`git status` fails), so approved-base comparison cannot be performed here. No new files are planned; all touchpoints below exist. Implementer verifies the normal checkout before changing them. Validation commands are planned, not executed during this artifact-only phase.

## Root cause and implementation sequence

1. Modify `internal/workflow/import_policy.go`, `recoveryReason`: replace the saved-patch suffix with wording such as “recovery patch <basename> was saved privately to your state directory; a maintainer may inspect the saved text and provide reviewed guidance through the existing work instruction flags.” Keep the existing retry command and role-output explanation from `importRejectionReason`. If naming flags, name only the verified `--instructions`, `--developer-instructions`, or `--tester-instructions` on the applicable work command. Do not interpolate patch text into commands. Avoid promises to retain/import other changes, automatic application, or authority/provenance. Preserve the unavailable and empty branches verbatim; keep basename-only projection. Retain the helper signature to avoid unrelated call-site churn.
2. Correct the three adjacent source comments listed above to describe private saved text for maintainer inspection, without claiming a recovery command exists. Do not change exported helpers, saving/loading logic, or policy.
3. Modify `internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go`: update old positive string expectations and add explicit absence checks for `recover-import` for both issue/PR saved guidance. Assert basename/private-state context, unchanged worktree, proper issue/PR work number and phase, role hints, and maintainer-reviewed guidance. Keep all existing privacy, patch-body/header, artifact, unavailable-patch and nonrecoverable assertions. Extend table coverage to PR unavailable and empty-patch cases without changing behavior.
4. Modify `internal/cli/import_rejection_test.go`: add a command-aware regression using the existing CLI fixture and rejecting-runner test seams where practical to obtain real emitted saved-rejection guidance, for issue and PR runs. Resolve each advertised command against `NewRootCmd()` using Cobra lookup; require exact `swarm issue work` / `swarm pr work` command path, executable leaf, and the expected remaining numeric argument. Assert every advertised flag is registered on that leaf and parse its argument vector without invoking RunE or any recovered content. Couple these checks to guidance assertions so stale invented commands fail. Include negative lookup coverage showing issue/pr recover-import are absent; a parent fallback must not count as success. Never use successful `unknown --help` exit status as evidence of registration. If existing seams cannot produce PR guidance cheaply, use the workflow table for actual PR emission and an explicitly matched CLI command/flag contract table, documenting that linkage in the test.
5. Run focused checks and required validation from TEST_PLAN.md. No recovered patch is executed or applied.

Only the four existing files above require changes. No docs, templates, commands, protected files, or recovery machinery need modification. Add a changelog fragment only if repository fragment validation requires one; do not widen product scope.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved inputs, gates, or validation.

- Entry points: `recoveryReason` (`internal/workflow/import_policy.go:204`), comments (`:25`, `:137`; `internal/agent/recovery.go:18`), guidance tests (`internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go:126`, `:201`), CLI tests (`internal/cli/import_rejection_test.go:10`). All files exist; none are new.
- Fixtures: `rejectingRunner` (`internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go:94`), `budgetEngine`, `newCLIFixture`, existing CLI PR fixtures. Extend existing fixture seams rather than production API surface.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/workflow -run 'Test(DeveloperOutput|ImportRejection|RejectedImport|CompletedTester|WritableImportPolicy|ImportPolicyRecoverable|Deletion)'`; `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestCLI.*Import'`; `go test ./internal/agent -run 'Test(Recovery|SaveRecovery)'`.
- Checked assumptions: searched all repository recover-import references and inspected real issue/PR command registrations and instruction flags. Cobra registration must be tested directly; help status is insufficient.
- Reopen if implementation requires command creation, patch execution, recovery format changes, new authority, changed fencing/ownership, or protected-file edits. Do not expand this fix to provide those capabilities.
- **What this change breaks**: positive unsupported-command expectations at `internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go:148`, `:211`, `:212` need replacement. Negative recover-import assertions at `internal/workflow/import_policy_test.go:382` and `internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go:194`, `:369` stay unchanged. Existing routing/completed-role tests, CLI status projection test, exported policy helper call sites, patch fixtures and privacy/fencing tests stay unchanged except additive coverage. Source comments naming the unsupported command get corrected as above. Search found no user docs/templates depending on that command. Preserve all real retry flags and eligible tester phase behavior.

# Test plan: saved-import recovery guidance

Implementation adds regression tests; this planning run only writes artifacts. Never execute recovered patch contents or run patch application commands.

## Acceptance coverage

| Acceptance criterion | Verification |
| --- | --- |
| Saved issue/PR guidance uses registered commands/flags, retains private-patch/retry context, and rejects unsupported suggestions | Extend `TestImportRejectionReasonWithPatch` for issue and PR saved, unavailable and absent patch cases. Assert private state-directory wording, exact basename without parent path, unchanged-worktree explanation, real numbered `work --phase implement` retries and maintainer-reviewed guidance; explicitly forbid recover-import and automatic import claims. Update `TestDeveloperOutputImportRecoveryGuidance`, retaining role-output instructions and saved metadata/body checks. Add `TestCLIImportRecoveryCommands` in the existing CLI test file: resolve advertised command paths on the actual root, require exact executable work leaves with expected numeric argument, look up and parse each advertised flag. Reject lookup that stops at issue/pr parent; verify recover-import has no registered leaf. Tie command/flag cases to the workflow guidance assertions or real emitted rejection fixture output. Old text must fail even if unknown-command help returns zero. |
| Unavailable, nonrecoverable/fork, role ownership, fencing and privacy stay unchanged; focused tests, make fmt/check pass | Preserve unavailable fixed-note and empty branches and test them for both routes. Run existing recoverability table (including fork), nonrecoverable saves-nothing tests, completed role and routing tests, deletion tests and rejection retry tests. Preserve local-error full-path versus projected-reason basename assertions and no-imported-artifact checks. Run agent private-storage, credential-withholding and bounds tests, plus existing stale-worker fencing tests and full race suite through make check. No saving/loading/policy code changes. |

## Focused commands

```bash
go test ./internal/workflow -run 'Test(DeveloperOutput|ImportRejection|RejectedImport|CompletedTester|WritableImportPolicy|ImportPolicyRecoverable|Deletion)'
go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestCLI.*Import'
go test ./internal/agent -run 'Test(Recovery|SaveRecovery)'
go test ./internal/workflow -run 'Test(WorkRepairStaleWorkerFailsWithClaimFence|BudgetPauseStillRequiresFence|BudgetCleanupExpiryDuringHandoffRemainsFenceError|ForkBudgetPauseWithoutUpstreamBudgetKeepsFence)'
```

Ensure the added CLI regression name matches the focused selector. Registration tests construct Cobra commands without executing work handlers, invoking agents, contacting GitHub, or running patch contents. During implementation, demonstrate the new unsupported-command regression fails against the old guidance and passes with the wording fix; preserve adversarial assertions.

## Required checks after implementation

```bash
make fmt
make check
go build ./...
go test ./...
```

`make check` includes formatting checks, vet, staticcheck, race-enabled tests and changelog validation. The last two commands also satisfy the compiled approved build/test checks explicitly. Use sandbox-writable build caches if needed; report unavailable dependencies or toolchain restrictions as validation limitations, not successful checks. Do not run formatter mutations in this read-only planning phase. No live GitHub, alternate platform, container runtime, or recovered-patch execution is required.

VERDICT: APPROVED

| Contract item | Audit |
| --- | --- |
| Guidance-only scope | Changes are limited to saved-rejection wording, inaccurate adjacent comments, and regression tests. No recovery command, patch application, permissions, format, authority, or provenance change is planned. |
| Registered issue/PR commands and flags | Verified root/issue/PR registration in internal/cli/root.go:123, issue.go:195, and pr.go:39–45. Work instruction and phase flags are registered in work.go:207–212 and pr.go:287–293. Planned tests require exact executable Cobra leaves, numeric arguments, and registered/parseable flags; parent help or a zero exit status cannot establish registration. |
| Useful retry and private-patch context | The plan retains numbered issue/PR work retries, eligible tester phase handling, unchanged-worktree and role-output explanations, private state-directory context, and filepath.Base projection. Maintainer inspection supplies reviewed guidance through existing flags without promising automatic import. |
| Unchanged rejection and security behavior | Unavailable/empty branches remain unchanged. Existing nonrecoverable/fork, ownership, private-storage, credential-withholding, bounds, artifact, and fencing coverage is retained. No saving/loading or policy logic is changed. |
| Acceptance verification | Both routes receive saved/unavailable/empty guidance coverage and unsupported-command assertions. Tests must fail against old guidance and directly verify Cobra registration. Focused tests, make fmt, make check, and approved build/test commands are planned. |
| Evidence and protected paths | PLAN.md factual citations match inspected source and tests. REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md repeats the design/test-plan evidence and contains no separate prior verdict or lesson requiring revision. No protected-path edits are planned. |

No blocking findings. The permitted matched workflow/CLI contract-table approach must retain the stated linkage to actual emitted guidance so an independently correct command table cannot mask an unsupported suggestion.

This is a plan review. Implementation tests and required checks were not run; their success remains to be established during implementation/validation. The snapshot lacks Git metadata, as the plan reports, so no approved-base diff was available.
